conclusions: The exact Host source requires the CM extension E/E+ unramified at every finite prime, including primes above 2. The conclusion does not replace this by a weaker conductor or character-count hypothesis.

Trace self-duality gives Lambda=J*Lambda_dual_h with J=xi^-1*Different(E/Q)^-1. If J=c*OE locally, the unimodular form is c^-1*h, not c*h. At an unramified quadratic place J has a scalar generator in F; the same c is used for every lattice under comparison.

A nondegenerate residue Hermitian form over the quadratic residue extension has a vector of nonzero norm even in characteristic 2, by the nonzero off-diagonal pairing and surjectivity of residue trace. Integral orthogonal splitting and surjective unit norms give the exact modular lattice classification. Split places use paired dual bases.

The rational isometry torsor belongs to U(h), whose derived group is simply connected SU(h) and whose quotient is Res_F/Q R^1_E/F Gm. The quadratic Hasse norm theorem verifies the quotient localization kernel, so Milne Lemma 8.20 proves the required rational isometry in every rank. Rank one reduces directly to the Hasse norm theorem.

The local determinant lift diag(v,1,...,1), transported through an integral basis, is unitary and congruent to identity modulo the full original m whenever v is. It works on the actual lattice and preserves both M and A labels, including their overlap.

The actual similitude quotient is T={(delta,c):delta*bar(delta)=c^n}. The signature uniform above K0 gives r(s)=(s^p*bar(s)^q,s*bar(s)); when p=q this is the base restriction of the smaller reflex field. Scalar u followed by the integral unitary determinant correction (bar(u)/u)^q lifts r(u) inside the original principal congruence subgroup.

For indefinite signatures the derived factors are real noncompact, so the connected-component theorem applies. The rational isometry calculation removes the extra PEL rational-class condition in Theorem 8.17, and Lan Remark 1.4.3.12 identifies the resulting characteristic-zero algebraic moduli action with the canonical model action. Passing through a smaller normal level does not change the final original level or field.

An automorphism fixing the K0 ray class field of modulus m has its Artin class represented by a finite unit idele congruent to 1 modulo m. Its infinite component may be taken to be 1. The exact reflex lift therefore kills its action on every connected component, not only on a selected component.

Definite signatures are treated independently: a rational E-orthogonal basis realizes the CM algebra E^n with conjugation Rosati involution and type induced from K0. No integral direct-sum decomposition of the original lattice or use of noncompact strong approximation at a definite endpoint is assumed.

The CM-algebra theorem yields the exact quasi-isogeny alpha(u*x)=sigma(x). Both it and its inverse preserve all integral Tate modules, hence are actual inverse isomorphisms. The central scalar commutes with the original E-action. Its congruence modulo m fixes every original finite label.

The polarization multiplier is explicitly rational by Milne 9.11(c), and is a finite unit because both cyclotomic character and Norm(u) are finite units. It is therefore +/-1; positivity of the two polarizations forces +1. The primitive graph construction then preserves the original rigidified line exactly. This normalization clarification was inserted during independent review with the author approval.

Characteristic-zero smoothness makes geometric irreducible components disjoint connected components. Their Galois invariance gives geometrically integral components over C*R_m. The exact source Omega is the fraction field of the polynomial ring in its original flag variables over the generic component field, so relative algebraic closedness extends to every quantified source element.

The ray-class exact sequence gives degree at most h(K0)*m^2, and the elementary reduced-form count gives h(K0)<=d for the actual prime d congruent 7 modulo 16. The conductor-discriminant formula gives rd(R_m)<=sqrt(d)*m. Normality over Q follows from conjugation-stability of the modulus; the cyclotomic inclusion follows from norm compatibility and the principal ray-unit congruence.

The stated compositum degree and root-discriminant bounds apply with R_m/Q Galois and yield fieldSz(C*R_m)<=fieldSz(C)+20*(log(m)+log(d)+1). For the actual good cover A=1 and m=g0*g1*15^e, exactly matching its source size and relative-normality clauses. There is no hidden degree factor from the growing field E.
